steps.title: It only looks even
steps.source: Very little is left on the board, and the position, to a beginner, probably looks absolutely even. It is not the case, however. Whoever has the move wins.

narration.say: To a beginner this looks absolutely even. It is not: whoever has the move wins.
The kings face each other with six squares between them. Even: so the player to move has the opposition.
The proper way to begin is to move straight up.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Go straight up.
exercise.success: 1. Ke2. Black does the same: Ke7.

steps.title: Your turn: keep the opposition
steps.source: Mere counting will show that the former course will only lead to a draw, therefore White takes the latter course.

narration.say: King to e3, king to e6. King to e4, and Black steps aside to f6.
White can pass with Kd5, or stop the black king from passing. Counting shows that passing only draws.

feedback.Kd5: Passing: Black passes too with Kg5, and counting shows it is only a draw.
feedback.*: Stand in front of the black king again.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Keep the opposition.
exercise.hint: The king goes to f4, face to face again.
exercise.success: 4. Kf4. Black goes to g6. If Ke6, then Kg5 wins.

narration.say: Now White passes: king to e5. Black to g7.
Counting shows that White wins by taking the pawn on b5.

steps.title: A waiting move
steps.source: Therefore it is seen that in such cases when the opponent makes a so-called waiting move, you must advance, leaving a rank or file free between the Kings.

narration.say: Black has a harder defence. King to e2, and Black waits with Kd8.
Now Kd3 is met by Kd7, and Ke3 by Ke7: Black gets the opposition.

feedback.Kd3: Black answers Kd7 and takes the opposition.
feedback.Ke3: Black answers Ke7 and takes the opposition.
feedback.*: There is only one other square forward.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Advance, leaving a file free between the kings.

steps.title: Your turn: back to the first line

narration.say: Now advancing would be bad. Play the same kind of move Black just played.

feedback.*: Put your king in front of the black king, on the same file.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Take the opposition.
exercise.wrong: Put your king in front of the black king, on the same file.
exercise.success: 3. Ke3. We are back in the first variation, and White wins.

narration.say: The opposition often decides the game.
Against a waiting move, advance, leaving a rank or file free between the kings.
